root_cause.text: The futex code incorrectly allocated and tracked the default `mm->futex_ref` hash only for `CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM` tasks, assuming pthread-style concurrency, so other `CLONE_VM` sharers could race the per-CPU futex reference setup and leave `mm->futex_ref` pointing at freed/per-CPU state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch says `need_futex_hash_allocate_default()` was “abusing CLONE_THREAD,” which “breaks the non-concurrency assumptions when doing the mm->futex_ref pcpu allocations,” causing “BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in futex_hash_put”; the fix changes the check from requiring `CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM` to any `CLONE_VM` clone except `vfork()` and removes the old “first thread spawns” logic in `copy_process()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust futex hash allocation to cover all non-vfork tasks sharing the parent's mm, not just CLONE_THREAD siblings.
intent_record.what: The function need_futex_hash_allocate_default() was rewritten from an if/return sequence that returned true only when both CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_VM were set, to a single վերադարձ expression that returns true when CLONE_VM is set and CLONE_VFORK is not set. A comment was added explaining that a default futex hash should be allocated for siblings sharing the parent's mm, except vfork.
intent_record.how: This changes the condition for allocating the default futex hash so it no longer requires CLONE_THREAD, and instead triggers whenever the new task will share the parent's memory map without being a vfork. That broadens the set of clone cases that get a default futex hash and avoids allocating it for vfork-created tasks.

It adds an explicit helper `need_futex_hash_allocate_default(u64 clone_flags)` that only returns true when `(clone_flags & (CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM)) == (CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM)`, and then allocates the default futex hash in `copy_process()` via `retval = futex_hash_allocate_default();`. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the incorrect allocation/tracking of `mm->futex_ref` only for `CLONE_THREAD | CLONE_VM` tasks without proper automatic allocation for the first thread; this snippet clearly introduces that allocation path and comments that it is for "the user process once the first thread spawns." Therefore the bug is not present here, and the fix is already present.
